subject: Supplier portal: invite token swapped / can't accept (Starlane)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@starlane.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: procure@starlane.com
Date: 2029-04-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Can't accept supplier invite — token appears swapped

Hi Michael,

We're trying to onboard our vendor user (alex@starlane.com) and the 'Accept Invitation' button returns a 401 with a message that the token belongs to a different account. We attached a screenshot of the error and a short video (see attachments).

Steps we took: open invite link, sign in with Google (alex@starlane.com), the page shows Starlane's organization but the Accept action fails and we see an account id that doesn't match our org.

This is blocking our PO visibility for today's cutover. Can you advise?

Thanks,
Tom
Procurement Ops — Starlane Manufacturing
attachments: screenshot-accept-button.png
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@starlane.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-05T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — token appears swapped

Hi Tom — thanks for the report and the screenshot, and sorry for the interruption here.

Quick ask while we investigate: can you forward the original invite URL (copy the full link from the email) and confirm whether Alex clicked the link from a corporate laptop or mobile? Also, please confirm the last 4 characters of the token that appears in the URL (we only need last 4 for correlation).

Workarounds you can try immediately (low risk):
- Open the invite link in an incognito/private browser window (this avoids any cross-account session cookies).
- If signing in with Google, use the account chooser to pick Alex's account explicitly rather than a cached session.

I've opened JIRA SUP-9823 and looped in Ben and Monica to check logs and whether the invite token was reissued or claimed by another email. We'll follow up with a short-lived override link if needed.

I'll keep you posted — target response within 2 hours.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-05T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — token appears swapped

Michael / Monica — ran a quick trace against SUP-9823. Observations:
- We saw an accept request at 2029-04-05T07:59:22Z that failed with 401. The bearer token in the Accept call maps to an account_id that belongs to an earlier invite from a different tenant (likely a stale cached token).
- The load balancer session affinity combined with our frontend cookie allowed the wrong session to persist when the user used a corporate browser with multiple signed-in identities.

Remediation plan:
1) Invalidate the current claim-token mapping for the Starlane invite (short-lived change).
2) Issue a one-time override invite URL (TTL 30 minutes) bound to alex@starlane.com.
3) Add a small client-side check to treat Accept requests from authenticated sessions that mismatch the invite email as a prompt to force re-auth (follow-up enhancement).

I attached the raw trace we pulled from the gateway. I'll generate the temporary link once Michael confirms we want to proceed.

ben
attachments: trace-log.txt
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@starlane.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-05T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — token appears swapped

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the patience. Per internal troubleshooting (included below), we invalidated the stale claim-token and generated a one-time override link for Alex. Steps: 
1) Open the attached temporary-login-link.txt and click the URL (link expires in 30 minutes).
2) Use an incognito/private window and explicitly sign in as alex@starlane.com.
3) If successful, you should see your Starlane PO list (we pushed a refresh for PO visibility).

Attached: temporary-login-link.txt (temporary URL), trace-log.txt (for our records).

Please confirm once Alex can accept and sees the PO. If it still fails I'll escalate to SRE for an immediate rollback of the token handler and we can reissue a fresh invite. Apologies for the extra steps — we'll also follow up to add the client-side prompt to prevent this in future.

Best,
Michael
Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
